example_prompt: In the Gozem sandbox, move my test delivery from pending to completed to check my webhook handler.

trip_id.description: Trip ID (TRP_xxx format or numeric ID) Path parameter.

action.description: Simulate trip state progression (assign driver, arrive at pickup, start trip, update location, complete trip). Which fields apply depends on action. Every branch takes action; the rest are only read for the actions that use them.

input_schema.description: Which fields apply depends on action. Every branch takes action; the rest are only read for the actions that use them.

data.description: The trip and its current state

driver.description: Driver handling the trip. Absent until one is assigned.

dropoffs.description: Delivery stops, in the order they are serviced

tracking_url.description: Public tracking URL that can be shared with the recipient. Contains a signed, short-lived JWT valid for the duration of the delivery.

code.description: Stable, machine-readable error code. Branch on this. See the Error Codes reference in the API description.

details.description: Field-level validation failures. Present on `validation_failed` only. API Basics types it object | array | null.

field.description: Dotted path to the offending field.

message.description: Human-readable message. May be reworded or localized — do not branch on it.

error.description: The HTTP error class name. Informational only; do not branch on it. (API Basics)

gotchas: Sandbox only: this endpoint doesn't exist in production, where trip state comes from the courier and the dispatch system.

One action per transition: assign (picks an available sandbox driver), arrive-pickup, start, then stop-start and stop-complete once per dropoff (they apply to the next undelivered one), then complete. cancel (optional reason) and expire are terminal, so each needs a fresh trip. update-location takes lat and lon (no state change); message takes sender_type (default driver; values not listed) and text.

Every transition returns the trip as it stands afterwards and fires the same webhook a real trip would: pause between calls and check your handler saw the event. Which event update-location fires, if any, isn't documented.
The client must be granted this endpoint in the sandbox portal like any other: there is no implicit access to related routes.

Authenticate with the x-api-key header: a long-lived API key that works only while its Partner Portal client is active. The docs recommend OAuth2 client credentials instead (POST https://auth.gozem.co/oauth2/token, then Authorization: Bearer; tokens last 3600 s by default). Send one credential per request — if both headers are present, the bearer token is used. Missing or invalid credentials return 401 unauthenticated; an endpoint the client wasn't granted, or a source IP outside its allowlist, returns 403 forbidden. How an API key is issued isn't documented: the Partner Portal flow described only generates a client_id and client_secret — ask your Gozem representative for the key.
trip_id is the trip's guid (TRP_…) or its numeric ID; an unknown trip returns 404 trip_not_found.

Failures share one envelope: branch on code — message is human-facing and may be reworded or localized. The API reference describes {success: false, code, message, details}, the API Basics page {error, message, code, details}: read only code, message and details (field-level failures on validation_failed; API Basics types details object, array or null). Statuses listed for this operation: 400, 401, 403, 404, 405, 409, 413, 415, 429, 500, 502. Retry only 429 rate_limit_exceeded (honour Retry-After; default limit 100 requests per minute per client; pace with the X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-RateLimit-Reset headers), 500 internal_error and 502 service_unavailable, with backoff.
